mechanism_narrative: The recent upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility, indicating a gradual return to pre-baseline activity levels, will continue to drive further increases in retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days, despite the observed upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility suggests growing public comfort with outdoor leisure, which will translate into higher RETAIL_REC within the next two weeks as people extend their outings.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, even if PARKS mobility rises by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility and an increase in GROCERY_PHARM visits signal a broader shift towards out-of-home activities, which will positively impact RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as people spend more time outside their homes.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility falling and GROCERY_PHARM mobility rising.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, even a slight recovery in WORKPLACES mobility indicates more people returning to physical offices, which will indirectly boost RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks due to increased weekday foot traffic.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES mobility shows any positive week-on-week change
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days, even if WORKPLACES mobility shows a positive week-on-week change in a reopening regime.

mechanism_narrative: A modest week-on-week increase in TRANSIT station mobility suggests a slight return of confidence in public transport, which will lead to a small but immediate positive impact on RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT mobility increases by more than 1 percentage point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next 7 days, despite TRANSIT mobility rising by more than 1 percentage point week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The combined effect of increasing PARKS mobility and decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility signifies a broader societal shift towards spending more time outside the home for leisure, which will directly boost RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases or remains flat over the next 14 days, despite PARKS mobility rising and RESIDENTIAL mobility falling.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high levels of PARKS mobility, indicative of favorable summer weather and outdoor activity, will continue to encourage people to leave their homes, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility remains consistently above -30% for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days, even if PARKS mobility remains consistently above -30%.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility shows no significant recovery (remaining below -50%) while RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated (above 10%), it indicates persistent work-from-home patterns that will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES mobility remains below -50% AND RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 10% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days, despite WORKPLACES mobility remaining below -50% and RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining above 10%.
